scripts.//preflight: check:all plus the two things that need more than a source tree: every test suite re-run under three timezones, and the LIVE schema probe. Nothing check-shaped is spelled out here any more, because a hand-copied subset is exactly how check:prose and check:decimals came to run nowhere.
scripts.preflight: npm run typecheck && npm run test:zones && npm run check:all && npm run check:schema
scripts.test:zones: TZ=Pacific/Kiritimati npm run test && TZ=Pacific/Auckland npm run test && TZ=Asia/Dubai npm run test && TZ=UTC npm run test && TZ=America/Los_Angeles npm run test && TZ=Pacific/Midway npm run test
scripts.//check:all: THE list of gates. Not a list, the list. Three entry points ran three different subsets of the check:* scripts and every difference was an accident nobody had decided on: preflight ran 17, scripts/publish.sh ran 15, .github/workflows/ci.yml ran 10. check:reachable, check:caps and check:roundtrip ran only at publish, so a branch could sit green in CI for a week carrying a screen nothing linked to. check:attribution and check:deltas ran only in preflight, which is the one of the three a person can forget to type, and check:attribution is the gate on a licence condition. Worst of the three, check:prose and check:decimals were wired into NOTHING: both scripts exist, both were written after a real report from a real gym floor, and no path in this repo ran either of them. A gate nobody runs is not a gate, it is a file. So every entry point now runs this one script and there is exactly one place to add the next check. The ONLY permitted asymmetry is upward and it is about credentials: everything here is a source read or a local build and needs no key, so it runs identically on a laptop, on a CI worker and immediately before an OTA. check:schema in its live form probes the real database and needs EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL plus the publishable key, so preflight and publish add it on top and CI holds no credentials and runs check:schema:offline, which is already in here. An entry point may run MORE than this list. None of them may run less, and nothing may be dropped from here to make a run go green.
scripts.check:all: npm run db:check && npm run check:native && npm run check:reads && npm run check:tabs && npm run check:portal && npm run check:trainer-profile && npm run check:traps && npm run check:attribution && npm run check:numbers && npm run check:contrast && npm run check:deltas && npm run check:currency && npm run check:catalogue && npm run check:caps && npm run check:prose && npm run check:decimals && npm run check:locale && npm run check:reachable && npm run check:roundtrip && npm run check:functions && npm run check:schema:offline && npm run check:bundle

//deferred-native-deps: Added at the dev-build/EAS stage (they require native code and do NOT run in Expo Go): @stripe/stripe-react-native
//native-deps-in-tree: Already installed and native, so a dev build is required from here on — Expo Go will not run the app: expo-video (exercise demos play inline; the alternative was Linking.openURL, which sends a client out of the app mid-session and is what lost their typed sets).
//react-native-health-patch: react-native-health 1.19.0 (last published Oct 2024, unmaintained) calls [self.callableJSModules setBridge:] in emitEventInternal, a selector RCTCallableJSModules no longer exposes in React Native 0.86 — so every iOS build under Expo SDK 57 failed to compile. The call is vestigial: RCTEventEmitter's own sendEventWithName:body: does not need the bridge set by hand. patches/ removes that one line and postinstall reapplies it, including on the EAS build server. Remove both if the package ever ships a fix.
